disease_label_per_paper: Polyarticular septic arthritis secondary to Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia after hemodialysis
presentation_summary: Male in his early 60s developed progressive polyarthralgia, difficulty walking, fever, and diaphoresis shortly after outpatient hemodialysis through a tunneled catheter.
Presentation vitals showed fever, borderline hypotension, tachycardia, hypoxemia, and multiple swollen warm painful joints including shoulders, ankles, knees, elbows, hands, MCP joint, and wrists.
Labs included CRP >300 mg/L, ESR 103 mm/hr, WBC 13.86 x10^9/L, creatinine 4.59 mg/dL, BUN 40 mg/dL, and eGFR 13 mL/min/1.72 m2.
Peripheral blood cultures grew MSSA, right knee drainage yielded opaque golden fluid with gram-positive cocci, and echocardiography showed a mobile mitral-valve density concerning for endocarditis.
